description: GPU build variants for the Windows desktop distribution. The stable CUDA build stays on the four-asset release channel; additional accelerator builds are independent previews because one PyTorch environment can only contain one accelerator runtime.

variants.name: cuda
requires: NVIDIA display driver with CUDA 12.4 support
variants.notes: Built by .github/workflows/release.yml as one of the four stable assets. CI compiles/loads the CUDA runtime and asserts sm_86 without a GPU; drawing the model on an RTX 3090 remains a real-hardware validation step.

variants.name: rocm
variants.torch_sha256_note: AMD's Windows preview index does not publish a per-wheel SHA-256; the HTTPS URL is pinned but the download is not hash-verified.
hardware: AMD Radeon GPU listed in AMD's ROCm on Windows compatibility matrix
requires: Python 3.12 embedded runtime (the AMD wheel is cp312-only)
variants.notes: AMD ships Windows ROCm PyTorch wheels only for CPython 3.12 (torch 2.9.1 at the time of writing), so this is a separate Python 3.12 build, not a drop-in torch swap in the Python 3.10 stable bundle. HIP exposes the torch.cuda API, so the existing inference device contract can use it, but no AMD hardware has run it in CI. The bundle must collect rocm_sdk and _rocm_sdk_* because torch/lib itself contains only 13 DLLs.

variants.name: xpu
hardware: Intel Arc / Intel Core Ultra integrated GPU
requires: Intel graphics driver supported by the XPU wheel
Intel GPU exposed as torch.xpu by torch 2.9.1+xpu
variants.notes: Official cp310 Windows XPU wheels exist. The shared core.torch_backend contract now resolves torch.xpu, uses torch.xpu.mem_get_info for VRAM admission and synchronizes XPU work, so this is a real Python 3.10 preview build. No Intel GPU has run it in CI; Conv3d/SDPA and the bundled model remain unverified on XPU.
